synopsis: UN R152 covers on-road car and van AEBS, not off-road machines; the identified edition is Revision 2 / 02 series (2024), published as EU OJ L 2024/2497 [f2821, f2526, f15400]. It requires a minimum commanded braking demand of 5.0 m/s², not measured deceleration, so the glossary's description of this as demanded deceleration needs qualification [f5993, f6307, f13632, f13951]. The corpus reports car-to-car testing at 10–60 km/h, pedestrian testing at 20–60 km/h and false-reaction scenarios, although one chapter passage explicitly says these reported details were not verified against the primary text [f2823, f2824, f2825, f2527, f2528, f2529]. January 2024 GRVA criticism identified incomplete virtual-testing credibility coverage, including insufficient physical evidence for individual toolchain components; the described method validates the toolchain against physical tests before use within its assessed envelope [f1279, f7690, f9746]. WP.29 adopted supplements in 2025 allowing virtual testing instead of some physical tests, while the text dated 28 August 2025 retains physical confirmation tests with their number agreed between manufacturer and authority [f7546, f7684]. The vendor-reported 30% physical-test minimum is not confirmed for the adopted text and should not be transferred to off-road machines without justification; a November 2025 Russian proposal for mandatory physical model verification also records continuing regulator-level debate [f7685, f7687, f7688, f7691].
